newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says rebel naval base destroyed.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says rebel naval base destroyed.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops attacked a northern rebel "Sea Tiger" naval base by sea and air, killing or wounding as many as 40 guerrillas, military officials said on Monday.
Sri Lankan forces lost five dead and 10 wounded in the assault on Sunday against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam's (LTTE) naval wing and the base was destroyed, a military spokesman said.
A spokesman for the LTTE said the attack was beaten off.

The Sea Tigers have emerged as a major threat to the navy and military convoys taking troops and supplies to bases in the north as the LTTE continues to fight for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
More than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year, according to govrenment figures.
"We hammered the base in a combined operation," the military spokesman said. "The Tigers withdrew after heavy fighting, making use of a good trench system. Our troops destroyed the base."
A navy boat and a Mi-17 helicopter were damaged in the attack on the Poonaithoduwai Sea Tiger base near the Jaffna peninsula, about 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo, he said.
The LTTE's Paris-based spokesman Lawrence Thilakar said rebel fighters repulsed the attack on what he called a Sea Tiger radar installation.
"A 40-ft long fast craft in which navy commandos came was sunk by LTTE fire," he said. "Another craft of similiar dimensions was badly damaged and a Mi-24 helicopter was also damaged."
Three rebels were killed and 10 navy commandos were believed to have died in the battle, he said.
The military spokesman said three senior rebels were among the dead, while a navy official said up to 40 LTTE rebels were believed killed or wounded.
Army special forces were landed by helicopter while the navy's Special Boat Squadron made an amphibious landing using shallow draught water-jet propelled boats, he said.
Army guns from a nearby base and navy gunboats offshore provided covering fire during the assault, military officials said.

Sri Lankan military officials said one of the navy water-jet vessels was sunk by rebel rocket-propelled grenades and another was badly damaged when sailors detonated a grenade which had failed to explode after hitting the craft.

The LTTE's Thilakar said air force Kfir jets, Pucara ground attack aircraft and Mi-24 helicopter gunships took part in the attack. He said several fishermen's cottages were burned down and a civilian was killed,
There was no way to verify Thilakar's statement independently since the government bans journalists from the war zone.
Army chief Lieutenant-General Rohan Daluwatte was quoted in the independent Island newspaper as saying the rebel base housed more than 1,000 guerrillas.
"This operation was conducted mainly to cripple the Sea Tiger strength in that area," he said.

Sunday's raid was the first major military offensive since last month's capture by the army of the rebel stronghold of Kilinochchi, the last major town held by the LTTE after the military regained control of the northern Jaffna peninsula in April.
